claims.text: All three platform artifacts describe one trip: trip_id TRP-00114 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix at 2026-08-07T18:40:00+08:00 matches the recorded start on the trip record. The rider has therefore carried limb (a) of the initial burden — the artifacts are of this trip and no identity objection is open.

The governing distance is the trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record: under POL-RD-01 gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two disagree, so the actual distance is 23.97 km against a booked optimal of 18.0 km — a measured excess of 5.97 km. The trip record's 24.0 km may not be cited for the threshold test.

Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass on those figures: the excess is 33.17% of the 18.0 km optimal route, above the 20% test, and 5.97 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km test. The route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace and limb (b) of POL-RD-08 is satisfied.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 241 fixes at a 10 second sample interval across 100% coverage, no gaps at all and max_gap_sec of 0.0, and no consecutive-fix jump anywhere near the 500 m limb. No independent corroboration is therefore required for the deviation and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

The only exculpatory route open to the driver is POL-RD-03, and it cannot run. I disclose that the artifact is impaired: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no payload — no LTA advisory covers the AYE, the PIE or the Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. POL-RD-03 needs a traffic_advisory naming an affected segment with an overlapping validity window; its absence is itself citable and it exonerates nothing. The driver's own statement concedes he knows of no advisory.

POL-RD-04 does not apply either. The two-message chat log shows the rider challenging the route — 'adam road?? jurong is the other way' at 18:58:40 — and the driver answering 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' at 18:59:20, which is an admission that the driver chose the corridor. There is no rider instruction, no named road requested by the rider, and waypoint_hint is null, so the rider-requested-detour clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

Nor was either endpoint amended: amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null and no pickup_amended_at or dropoff_amended_at is recorded, so POL-RD-05 has no amended re-quote to re-price the trip against and cannot excuse any part of the 5.97 km excess.

The fare model on this trip is METERED, so the remedy is the arithmetic of POL-RD-02, not a discretionary payment. Recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30) x 1.6) + 0.80 + 2.50 = (25.70 x 1.6) + 3.30 = 41.12 + 3.30 = 44.42, where 1.6 is the surge_multiplier read from the fare breakdown (the rider does not contest the surge) and 2.50 is the ERP of the single gantry lying on the optimal route, the Kim Keat Link gantry.

Charged_total is 58.10, so the refund is 58.10 less 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 as SGD 13.70. That is comfortably above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome for this rider-filed dispute is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 13.70, leaving the rider not carrying the charge for the six kilometres he never asked for.

The SGD 2.00 Adam Road gantry — the off-optimal-route line — is ALREADY comprehended in that refund under POL-RD-09(1), because the recomputed fare carries only the on-route Kim Keat Link gantry: the difference between the 4.50 actually billed and the 2.50 recomputed sits inside the 13.68. It is itemised for transparency and must never be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure. The 2.50 on-route gantry properly stands.

No escalation trigger fires on this record. The trace is clean, the trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and the driver's congestion assertion cites no artifact at all — POL-RD-08 says a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. That is an undischarged defence, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, which requires an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool. The record is sufficient to move money and the case should be ruled, not held.

The rider's own profile does not trigger the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, not 4 or more, so no independent source beyond the trace is required for this claim. I cite only that field, for the test that names it.

The established deviation is not additionally MATERIAL: 5.97 km is 33.17%, below the 50% test, and below the 8.0 km absolute test. No POL-RD-06 driver-profile pattern finding is sought and none is needed — the rider's remedy rests entirely on this trip's own trace and the fare arithmetic, and no adverse finding is built on either party's reputation.

claims.text: On this trip's own trace a route deviation is established, and I do not contest it: the governing GPS polyline measures 23.97 km against the 18.0 km booked optimal, an excess of 5.97 km or 33.17%, which clears both POL-RD-01 gates (20% and 0.8 km). What the same figures do not do is reach MATERIALITY — that requires an excess above 50% of optimal (9.0 km) or above 8.0 km absolute, and 5.97 km fails both. This is an ordinary, not a material, deviation, so POL-RD-06's driver_profile consultation and its FULL_REFUND uplift are not engaged on this trip.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be built here, on the only figures POL-RD-06 permits. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 412 — a ratio of 0.24%, far below the 0.05 ratio the clause requires, and a raw flag count far below the 3 it also requires. The uplift to FULL_REFUND and the conduct referral therefore both fall away. The lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is a different quantity and is context only; POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting it for the trailing-90-day figure.

The 1.6 surge is properly chargeable and belongs to no refund. fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier is 1.6 and, on this rate card, applies to base, distance and time only — never to the 4.50 of ERP — and POL-RD-02 requires the multiplier to be read from the fare_breakdown and carried into any recomputed fare. The 19.80 surge line therefore stands whatever else is decided, and no part of it is recoverable by the rider.

The 2.00 Adam Road gantry lies off the optimal route, but under POL-RD-09(1) that charge is already comprehended in any POL-RD-02 recomputation — which credits only gantries lying on the optimal route — and it must never be itemised as a separate correction and then added on top of the refund as a second recovery. By contrast the 2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry does lie on the optimal route and is properly chargeable; the trip record confirms the optimal route crosses that gantry and nothing else.

There is no phantom-gantry billing-integrity correction available under POL-RD-09(4). The unbroken 100%-coverage trace passes within 250 m of both billed gantries — 0.0 m from the Kim Keat Link gantry and 8.76 m from the Adam Road gantry — so both lines are matched crossings of gantries the vehicle actually drove through, and neither may be refunded as an unmatched line.

The only explanation the driver offers for leaving the optimal corridor — that the AYE was crawling from the Alexandra exit — is a traffic ground under POL-RD-03, and the artifact that clause requires is absent from the pool: EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0, and no LTA advisory covers the AYE, PIE or Alexandra corridor in the 18:36-19:20 window. An exculpatory ground asserted against an artifact missing from the pool is a POL-RD-10(5) trigger, and with the advisory absent the record cannot test the driver's explanation either way. The disputed amount should be held for a human reviewer under POL-RD-10 rather than resolved against the driver on an empty record. Disclosure under POL-GEN-02: the advisory artifact relied on here is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT.

ruling.explanation:
Decision on trip TRP-00114 (Bugis Junction → Jurong East MRT), addressed to both of you.

THE DEVIATION IS ESTABLISHED. The platform's booked optimal route was 18.0 km. The GPS trace actually driven measures 23.97 km, an excess of 5.97 km — 33.2% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km). The trip record's '24.0 km' is a rounded copy of the same measurement and may not be used for the threshold test; the trace figure governs. The driver does not contest this and the trace is clean (241 fixes, 10 s interval, no gaps), so no corroboration rule is engaged.

NOT MATERIAL, SO NO UPLIFT OR REFERRAL. 33.2% is below the 50% materiality test and 5.97 km is below the 8.0 km absolute test. POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged: the driver-profile check produces no pattern (deviation_flags_90d = 1 over completed_trips_90d = 412), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral. No other profile field has been used against either of you.

NO EXCULPATION. POL-RD-03 (road-closure/advisory) cannot run: the required traffic advisory is absent from the pool — EV-ADVIS-00114-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — and the driver's own account concedes he knows of no advisory. His 'AYE was crawling' explanation is a general assertion that traffic was bad and cites no artifact; under POL-RD-08 that does not discharge his burden. It is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, because that trigger needs an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool, and the driver points to no advisory artifact at all. POL-RD-04 does not apply (the chat log shows the rider challenging the route, not requesting one, and waypoint_hint is null), and POL-RD-05 does not apply (no amended endpoints and both amended_optimal fields are null).

THE FARE ARITHMETIC (METERED trip, POL-RD-02):
- optimal inputs: 18.0 km, 30.0 min; surge multiplier 1.6 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (base, distance and time only; never ERP).
- recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75×18.0 + 0.28×30.0) × 1.6) + 0.80 + 2.50 = (25.70 × 1.6) + 3.30 = 41.12 + 3.30 = 44.42.
- charged_total = 58.10.
- refund = 58.10 − 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 13.70.
That is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and well below 90% of charged_total, hence PARTIAL_REFUND.

The 1.6 surge stands and is not refunded. The $2.00 Adam Road gantry is off the optimal route, but under POL-RD-09(1) it is already comprehended inside the 13.70 and is itemised here only for transparency — it is not added on top. The $2.50 Kim Keat Link gantry lies on the optimal route and is properly chargeable. There is no phantom-gantry billing defect: the trace passes within 250 m of both billed gantries, so both are genuine crossings and POL-RD-09(4) gives no separate refund or referral.

NO ESCALATION. The trace is unimpaired, the trip identifiers match across all three platform artifacts, no timestamps disagree or run backwards, no charge line lacks a counterpart, and the refund does not exceed the charged total. The only missing artifact (the advisory, weight 0.0) carries no deciding fact, so the confidence cap is set by the artifacts that do — the trace, trip record and fare breakdown, all at weight 1.0. Confidence 0.88, above the 0.70 floor. The disputed amount is not held; SGD 13.70 is refunded to the rider and SGD 44.42 is the corrected amount payable for the trip.
